statBlock.name: Ancient Brass Dragon
statBlock.description: An outspoken desert dragon whose lair is surrounded by mirages and magically refreshing water.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (4/day, or 5/day in its lair). On a failed save, the dragon can spend a use to succeed.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. The dragon can use Sleep Breath or cast Scorching Ray at level 3 through Spellcasting in place of one attack.
Rend. Melee attack, +14 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. line 5 ft. wide makes a DC 21 Dexterity save. Failure deals 58 (13d8) Fire damage. Success halves the damage.
Sleep Breath. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 21 Constitution save. On failure, the creature is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn and repeats the save then. On a second failure, it falls Unconscious for 10 minutes. Damage wakes it, as does an action taken by a creature within 5 ft.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells takes an action. The dragon uses Charisma (save DC 20), and the spells require no Material components.
Scorching Ray uses a +12 spell attack bonus, calculated from Charisma and proficiency.
At will. Detect Magic, Minor Illusion, Scorching Ray at level 3, Shapechange, Speak with Animals.
1/day each. Control Weather, Detect Thoughts.
Shapechange only allows Beast or Humanoid forms. It grants no Temporary Hit Points and requires neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 uses, or 4 in its lair. It can spend one use on one option immediately after another creature’s turn. Spent uses return at the start of the dragon’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Blazing Light. Cast Scorching Ray at level 3 through Spellcasting.
Pounce. Move up to half its Speed and make one Rend attack.
Scorching Sands. A visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 20 Dexterity save. On failure, it takes 36 (8d8) Fire damage and its Speed is halved until the end of that creature’s next turn. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
sections.Lair resources: The encounter is worth 33,000 XP in the lair. The dragon has 5 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses there.
sections.Regional effects:
Mirages. From its lair the dragon can cast Major Image without Material components, using its Spellcasting ability. The range is 1 mile, and the effect can appear in places the dragon cannot see.
Refreshing Water. A creature that drinks water from within 1 mile of the lair gains 2d4 Temporary Hit Points. The dragon immediately knows the drinker is present.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 56. Includes the regional effects.

statBlock.name: Ancient Bronze Dragon
statBlock.description: An amphibious coastal dragon that can stir the weather around its lair and ease the passage of swimmers.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes both air and water.
Legendary Resistance (4/day, or 5/day in its lair). On a failed save, the dragon can spend a use to succeed.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. The dragon can use Repulsion Breath or cast Guiding Bolt at level 2 through Spellcasting in place of one attack.
Rend. Melee attack, +16 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit 18 (2d8 + 9) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Lightning damage.
Lightning Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 120-ft. line 10 ft. wide makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 82 (15d10) Lightning damage. Success halves the damage.
Repulsion Breath. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 23 Strength save. On failure, push the creature up to 60 ft. straight away from the dragon and knock it Prone.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells takes an action. The dragon uses Charisma (save DC 22, +14 to hit with spell attacks), and the spells require no Material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Guiding Bolt at level 2, Shapechange, Speak with Animals, Thaumaturgy.
1/day each. Detect Thoughts, Control Water, Scrying, Water Breathing.
Shapechange only allows Beast or Humanoid forms. It grants no Temporary Hit Points and requires neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 uses, or 4 in its lair. It can spend one use on one option immediately after another creature’s turn. Spent uses return at the start of the dragon’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Guiding Light. Cast Guiding Bolt at level 2 through Spellcasting.
Pounce. Move up to half its Speed and make one Rend attack.
Thunderclap. Center a 20-ft.-radius sphere on a visible point within 120 ft. Each creature in that sphere makes a DC 22 Constitution save. On failure, it takes 13 (3d8) Thunder damage and is Deafened until the end of that creature’s next turn.
sections.Lair resources: The encounter is worth 50,000 XP in the lair. The dragon has 5 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses there.
sections.Regional effects:
Buoying Currents. Within 1 mile of the lair, creatures without a Swim Speed can swim without paying the usual extra movement cost.
Sun and Storms. In its lair, the dragon can cast Control Weather without Material components, using its Spellcasting ability. This casting controls weather within 1 mile of the lair and works whether the dragon is indoors or outdoors.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 60. Includes the regional effects.

statBlock.name: Ancient Copper Dragon
statBlock.description: A mischievous dragon whose presence gives small animals the power of speech and leaves intruders helpless with laughter.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (4/day, or 5/day in its lair). On a failed save, the dragon can spend a use to succeed.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. The dragon can use Slowing Breath or cast Mind Spike at level 5 through Spellcasting in place of one attack.
Rend. Melee attack, +15 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Acid damage.
Acid Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. line 10 ft. wide makes a DC 22 Dexterity save. Failure deals 63 (14d8) Acid damage. Success halves the damage.
Slowing Breath. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 22 Constitution save. On failure, its Speed is halved, it cannot take Reactions, and it must choose between an action and a Bonus Action on its turn. These effects last until the end of the creature’s next turn.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells takes an action. The dragon uses Charisma (save DC 21), and the spells require no Material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Mind Spike at level 5, Minor Illusion, Shapechange.
1/day each. Greater Restoration, Major Image, Project Image.
Shapechange only allows Beast or Humanoid forms. It grants no Temporary Hit Points and requires neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 uses, or 4 in its lair. It can spend one use on one option immediately after another creature’s turn. Spent uses return at the start of the dragon’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Giggling Magic. A visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 21 Charisma save. On failure, it takes 31 (9d6) Psychic damage and subtracts 1d8 from each ability check and attack roll it makes until the end of the creature’s next turn. Roll that d8 for each check or attack. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Mind Jolt. Cast Mind Spike at level 5 through Spellcasting. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. Move up to half its Speed and make one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: The encounter is worth 41,000 XP in the lair. The dragon has 5 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses there.
sections.Regional effects:
Chatty Critters. Tiny Beasts can magically speak and understand Draconic while within 6 miles of the lair.
Giggle Fits. When a creature other than the dragon or one of its allies rolls a 1 on a D20 Test within 1 mile of the lair, it makes a DC 15 Wisdom save. On failure, laughter leaves it Incapacitated until the end of its next turn.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 80. Includes the regional effects.

statBlock.name: Ancient Gold Dragon
statBlock.description: An amphibious dragon that sends messages through dreams and hides its lair in warning fog.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The dragon breathes both air and water.
Legendary Resistance (4/day, or 5/day in its lair). On a failed save, the dragon can spend a use to succeed.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. The dragon can cast Guiding Bolt at level 4 through Spellcasting or use Weakening Breath in place of one attack.
Rend. Melee attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit 19 (2d8 + 10) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Fire damage.
Fire Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 24 Dexterity save. Failure deals 71 (13d10) Fire damage. Success halves the damage.
Weakening Breath. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone that is free of this breath’s effect makes a DC 24 Strength save. On failure, it has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests and subtracts 5 (1d10) from its damage rolls. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. A success ends the effect, and the save succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells takes an action. The dragon uses Charisma (save DC 24, +16 to hit with spell attacks), and the spells require no Material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Guiding Bolt at level 4, Shapechange.
1/day each. Flame Strike at level 6, Word of Recall, Zone of Truth.
Shapechange only allows Beast or Humanoid forms. It grants no Temporary Hit Points and requires neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 uses, or 4 in its lair. It can spend one use on one option immediately after another creature’s turn. Spent uses return at the start of the dragon’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Banish. A visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 24 Charisma save. On failure, it takes 24 (7d6) Force damage, is Incapacitated, and is sent to a harmless demiplane until the start of the dragon’s next turn. The dragon then chooses an unoccupied space within 120 ft. of the dragon where the creature reappears. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Guiding Light. Cast Guiding Bolt at level 4 through Spellcasting.
Pounce. Move up to half its Speed and make one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: The encounter is worth 75,000 XP in the lair. The dragon has 5 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses there.
sections.Regional effects:
Dream Messenger. In its lair, the dragon can cast Dream using Charisma and without Material components. This casting can target any creature within 6 miles.
Foretelling Fog. Opalescent fog leaves the area within 1 mile of the lair Lightly Obscured. Creatures in the fog cannot be surprised because its shifting shapes warn them of danger.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 146. Includes the regional effects.

statBlock.name: Ancient Silver Dragon
statBlock.description: A mountain and city dragon that can control the weather from its lair. Winds nearby catch falling creatures.

sections.Traits: Legendary Resistance (4/day, or 5/day in its lair). On a failed save, the dragon can spend a use to succeed.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three Rend attacks. The dragon can use Paralyzing Breath or cast Ice Knife at level 2 through Spellcasting in place of one attack.
Rend. Melee attack, +17 to hit, reach 15 ft. Hit 19 (2d8 + 10) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Cold damage.
Cold Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 24 Constitution save. Failure deals 67 (15d8) Cold damage. Success halves the damage.
Paralyzing Breath. Each creature in a 90-ft. cone makes a DC 24 Constitution save. On failure, it is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn and repeats the save then. On a second failure, it is Paralyzed and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. A success ends the effect, and the save succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
sections.Spellcasting:
Casting one of these spells takes an action. The dragon uses Charisma (save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks), and the spells require no Material components.
At will. Detect Magic, Hold Monster, Ice Knife at level 2, Shapechange.
1/day each. Control Weather, Ice Storm at level 7, Teleport, Zone of Truth.
Shapechange only allows Beast or Humanoid forms. It grants no Temporary Hit Points and requires neither Concentration nor Temporary Hit Points to maintain.
sections.Legendary actions:
The dragon has 3 uses, or 4 in its lair. It can spend one use on one option immediately after another creature’s turn. Spent uses return at the start of the dragon’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Chill. Cast Hold Monster through Spellcasting. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Cold Gale. Each creature in a 60-ft. line 10 ft. wide makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. On failure, it takes 14 (4d6) Cold damage and is pushed up to 30 ft. straight away from the dragon. Success halves the damage and prevents the push. The dragon can use this option again starting on its next turn.
Pounce. Move up to half its Speed and make one Rend attack.
sections.Lair resources: The encounter is worth 62,000 XP in the lair. The dragon has 5 daily Legendary Resistance uses and 4 legendary action uses there.
sections.Regional effects:
Gentle Gusts. A creature falling within 1 mile of the lair descends at 60 ft. per round and takes no falling damage.
Sun and Storms. In its lair, the dragon can cast Control Weather without Material components, using its Spellcasting ability.
Both effects end immediately if the dragon dies or moves its lair.
sections.Printed source: Monster Manual (2024), p. 280. Includes the regional effects.
